title: Traffic constriction and lazy fallback heuristics for regional routing
creator: Priya Singh
description: Design and implement a lightweight, score-driven fallback mechanism that performs gradual traffic constriction ("lazy fallback") and hard circuit-breaker actions across regions and tiers. The goal is to reduce blast radius from 429 storms, timeouts, and error-rate spikes while minimizing unnecessary full cutovers. This ticket covers the heuristics, telemetry signals, Router integration points, and runtime knobs for operators.
acceptance_criteria: Fallback decision uses a multi-signal trip score (429 rate, timeout count, p95 latency, error_rate) computed per route+region+tenant and persists state across short windows
Traffic constriction supports stepped percentage reductions (e.g., 10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with configurable hold and decay windows
Soft-fallback (route to quantized/cheaper model variant) and hard-fallback (regional cutover) are emitted as distinct actions and recorded in event logs
Circuit-breaker exposes 4 states (Closed, Constricting, Open, Probation) with clear transition rules and admin override via feature flag
Telemetry dashboards show trip_score, state, decision_reason, and rollback events; alerts fire on >3 probation failures within 1h
Unit and integration tests cover signal aggregation, hysteresis, grace windows, and edge cases (burst vs sustained errors)
Staged canary rollout completed in staging and production with documented rollback steps
design_decisions: Use a decaying additive trip score rather than a monolithic threshold to combine signals — easier to tune across workloads
Signals: 429_rate (per-minute), timeout_count (per-minute), p95_latency (5m rolling), error_rate (5m rolling). Map each to a contribution weight configurable per route
Hysteresis with asymmetric ingress/egress windows: require sustained signal for longer to open compared to shorter window to close (e.g., open: 3m sustained, close: 1m sustained)

Two-phase fallback actions: (1) constrict traffic percentage to lower tiers/variants, (2) escalate to regional handoff or Open circuit. Constriction acts as probation and lowers impact while testing stability
Per-tenant and per-route scopes supported; global defaults provided. Tenant overrides stored in config service with audit trail
State store will be centralized Redis cluster for fast reads/writes with TTLs to avoid stale opens across redeploys
Router integration point: decision endpoint that returns (action, target_variant, new_percentage, reason_tag) and Router applies instant-percentage sampling without rebalancing other routes
implementation_notes: Create new component 'trip-controller' in routing-service responsible for scoring and state transitions
Metric names: routing.trip_score, routing.fallback_state, routing.constriction_pct, routing.decision_reason (tagged by route, region, tenant)
Config knobs: weights per-signal, open_threshold, constrict_steps (array), hold_duration_ms, decay_half_life_ms, probation_duration_ms
Persist state as flattened keys: <route>::<region>::<tenant>::state and <route>::<region>::<tenant>::score in Redis; avoid nested JSON
Expose admin REST endpoints: GET /trip/<route>, POST /trip/<route>/override, DELETE /trip/<route>/clear
Feature-flag behind 'routing.lazy_fallback' with rollout via console; default off for high-risk customers
Add graceful backoff for control-plane write thrash: batch writes to Redis with 500ms coalescing
Integrate with existing rollout and tracing: annotate traces with trip_decision_id and link to check-run logs
Add a quick-toggle that converts constriction to simulated mode (decision logged but not enforced) for observability during tuning
test_plan: Unit tests for trip scoring math and signal weight changes
Simulated k6 load tests generating 429 storms and timeout bursts across two regions to validate constriction steps
Chaos test: kill a model pool to induce timeouts and verify regional probation and subsequent reopen rules
A/B canary: run simulated traffic with simulated decisions (simulate mode) to verify decision distribution and false positives
Regression: verify existing router path selection unchanged when feature flag disabled
Runbook drill: ops run through a pre-recorded incident where constriction saved capacity and prevented full failover
Monitoring asserts: dashboard panels for p95, trip_score, constriction_pct, and time-to-recovery; automated replay of saved traces
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit+integration tests, local Redis emulation
Phase 1 (staging): enable routing.lazy_fallback in staging, simulated mode for 48h, tune weights
Phase 2 (canary): enable in prod for internal customers and 5% traffic live for 24h, monitor key metrics
Phase 3 (incremental): 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 7 days if no regressions; each step hold for 24h
Phase 4 (ops handoff): create runbook, alert thresholds, and grant on-call the override endpoint
Rollback: immediate feature-flag off; run Redis clear command to remove all constriction states if necessary
risks_mitigation: False positives: mitigate by conservative default weights and simulated mode before enforcement
State inconsistency: use TTLs and short decay windows; provide admin clear endpoint
Overreaction to transient spikes: stepped constriction with probation minimizes full cutovers
Performance overhead: batch Redis writes and limit scoring frequency to once per 10s per route
Security: admin endpoints secured with SSO + audit logs; no sensitive data persisted
